newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian airlines latest to add cargo surcharges.
newsitem.headline: Canadian airlines latest to add cargo surcharges.

text.p: Canadian Airlines International plans to start charging a fuel surcharge on all domestic and international cargo shipments, effective Nov 25, a spokesman told Reuters.
Jon Shaw said the domestic surcharge will be C$0.05 cents/kg, while international shipments will be subject to a C$0.12 cents/kg surcharge, regardless of origin or destination.
These surcharges and the implementation date are identical to increases announced Friday by CAI's part-owner, American Airlines, for ex-Canada routings.
Meanwhile, Air Canada is expected to announce a fuel surcharge on westbound North Atlantic lanes starting Nov 15, an industry source told Reuters.

This surcharge, to apply to Europe-to-Canada routes, will be the equivalent of US$0.10 cents/kg as converted into the local currency of the originating market - 6 pence in the UK, 15 pfennig in Germany, 50 centimes in France.
The source said Air Canada is hedging on matching CAI's surcharge on transpacific routes because none of the major Asian carriers serving Vancouver or Toronto have announced a surcharge of their own.

From Canada to Europe, Air Canada is said to be reluctant to apply a surcharge until year-end because of existing price commitments to major freight forwarder customers. -Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
